nodes.title: director37: 36 lessons on round d37's candidate before release, nine judges: nine of nine topics pass every gate line; 880 keyed answers, 0 misgrades, 0 false keys, 0 contradictions, 0 unsaid boards; register 3.5 in nine of nine; listening up in three topics, no axis down

After director37: release 63 is candidate 8354c9855 with six lessons live; the next walk change is the four-hearing cap only; Learning 025 comes before any further walk round on register; then one lesson rewritten whole to a written description of a 4
A turn that opens on her reply to a side-topic and has a new point is reply, joint, the whole point and the point's check-in; the card is the next turn
The first teaching turn after two requests is start line, hook, whole point and check-in; the card is the next turn
A clarify at the check-in of a held card gets help on the point and the held card in one turn

A waiting child hears the question: wait one a short ask, wait two the re-ask, wait three help ending on the question, wait four tells; never two turns running with no question; a try-first is a request; the child's words are recorded as said

On a two-topic pair measure a gated flag outside the cause under test is disclosed to the judge, logged and assigned and does not hold the measure; one inside the cause holds it; no lesson is re-run to clear a flag
A cause the rule-based children do not reach is accepted on an independent review of its predicates and an as-heard read of driven walks, not on a paid pair run

A told own-step answer is the step's answer with its own reason; where the reason names every number of the answer the reason alone is said; at the cap a named wrong answer's unsaid reason is said with one more try
A return led by a verdict opens on a back-to word where the script has one; a park of something the child told is always returned to; the AI line never asks what the child's question named

After the last builder of a round, readers who built nothing read all lessons of the final offline walk against the walk the round started from before the paid run; a rule is kept only on a measure in which it fired; the whole director and script test set runs after the last builder
A plain "nahi" at any comprehension check-in is read as "I did not understand" and takes that path
Every reply to a child's "let me try" is "Haan, pehle tum try karo." and nothing after it; the turn after the go-ahead is wait one if the child does not answer
c4-maths-ch05-t01 runs its rewritten script with the one wording that failed director36 put back to its director35 text
Turn 12 of the stuck lessons stays as built: help in the point's wording ending on the card's short question that the help two turns before also ended on
A picture the child asked for, after the no-other-drawing line, stays through the card when the card's board is the same figure (director37 ruling 5)
c4-maths-ch06-t01 has two passing runs but does not go live in release 63; it goes live after its two script rows are fixed and read and the script passes the live-only rules (director37 ruling 4)
d37 cause A, design D1, on two topics (8 lessons, 2 judges): gates clean, register 3.5 unchanged, turns over 70 words from 6 to 1; the go-on turn after a reply heard as dead in 8 of 8

d37 cause A, design D2, on the same two topics (8 lessons, 2 judges): reply, point and check-in turns of 47 to 58 words judged better than both earlier shapes; gates clean, axes unchanged; one gated flag outside the cause
d37 offline matrix after causes A and B, before cause C (36 lessons, no model): turns over 70 words from 22 to 6, check-in endings from 84 to 150, two check-ins running from 8 to 32
d37 offline matrix after the harness fix 1ca1546e6: no wait longer than two of her turns in any of 36 lessons (director36 live: eleven and six)
d37 offline matrix before and after cause C (36 lessons, no model): keys told from 29 to 21, values said twice in a told answer from 13 to 0, the cap before an unsaid named reason from 6 to 0
d37 cause C on two topics (8 lessons, 2 judges, $0.49): gates clean, nothing gated, no safety turn; C1, C2 and C3 kept with two corrections; register 3.5 unchanged
d37 offline matrix at the close, against the round start (36 lessons, no model): turns over 70 words from 22 to 5, check-in endings from 84 to 132, told answers from 20 to 17
d37 first whole read: three Opus readers, all 36 lessons of the closing walk against the round start: all three said no; four regressions of the round's own, four smaller new faults, four older ones
d37 second whole read: three fresh Opus readers, 36 lessons: yes (0 faults in 441 turns), yes (11 B rows in 477), no on one fault (the try-first tail); every item of the first read's ruling gone

d37 offline matrix after the fixes of the first whole read, against the round start (36 lessons, no model): turns over 70 words from 22 to 17, check-in endings from 84 to 135, go-on turns with no question from 5 to 3; 189 gated checks all 0
Ending her reply's turn on a back-to-work line with no question (design D1): both judges heard a dead turn in 8 of 8; the off-topic child filled it with more side-topics
Measuring a cause by "register rows under length or shape halve": judges list exactly five rows a lesson, so rows only move between causes while the score stays 3.5
Letting a builder change a gated check it builds against: one exempted the row a reader then faulted, three loosened readings beyond their ruling
Writing a round's cause for director36's "wait with no end" before knowing it was largely the rule-based child not recognising the question in her re-ask or help
Rewriting a waiting child's "haan" to "pata nahi" so the help picker treats it as a give-up: the rewrite reached the talk monitor, the persona signals and the recorded words
Counting a try-first as a wait turn: "mujhe khud try karne do" was answered with a hint
Ruling cause A's design D2 before reading director28 and director29, which had already faulted a check-in after an aside reply
Briefing a background builder without limiting its tools: it stalled 20 minutes on an MCP permission prompt nobody could answer
Dropping the remediation's wordings at a follow-up card (C5) to cure one judged row: it took away 22 help turns and the answer was told after one hint
Saying a script's short reason after a told answer (C6): the short reason is the same reason cut short, so it repeated the answer (3 of 3)
Dropping the worked problem's easier wording from an own step's help (C4): it left "this is the simplest way I have" untrue
Ruling three of cause C's six rules from the order's text: none survived an as-heard read of the offline walk; none reached a paid run
Splitting a return from its verdict as a go-on turn where the script has no back-to form (D1's fallback): dead on 16 of 23 returns
Keeping the worked close split from its card (A(iii)) on a pair measure in whose topics it never fired: it made a turn with no question in every lesson of two topics
Rule-based children that answer a yes-or-no check-in with "pata nahi, aap batao" and never "nahi": a plain no passed over as a yes was invisible to every walk
Saying the reply turn's point over the held card's board: four unsaid-board rows that no gated check read, found by the whole read
Running 402 test files one at a time in a builder's worktree: over an hour, cut at 332
Meeting "never two turns running with no question" by adding a short ask or an invitation after "Haan, pehle tum try karo.": the check read 0 and the child who asked to be left alone was nudged
Each builder running only "the tests my item touches": tests/r8-main-034 failed from the closing pass on and no builder ran it
A builder command with an empty shell variable: it wrote a note in "/" and its "rm" needed a permission nobody could give (10 minutes lost)
The four-hearing cap as built after d37: the told answer came at the cap with a wording still unsaid in four lessons, and one step question was heard eight times before it was told

Script rows found in round d37 for Learning 025, not changed in the round: c5-ch02-t03 a card's Hindi form said cold; c6-ch07-t01 s1 pointAlt repeating the hook's image, its first card's simpler/prompt doubled lead and overlapping help wordings; c4-ch06-t01 "chhota khaana" as 1 cm then 10 cm and a helpSpent form ending "koi baat nahi" before help.js's own; "Ab tak samajh aaya?" after two not-understoods; ASIDE_AGAIN "maine likh li hai"; "Tumhari baari:" heard again three turns after the told step; rows under pending thenHelpOtherBoard (22) and ownStepWorkedHelp (2); teach-back keys saying the value twice (steady c5-ch02-t02 116, steady c6-ch06-t01 98); "Sana ka hissa" twice in c5-ch02-t02's own-step key and reason; replyKinds person forms "Arre wah, X!" and "Oho, X!" heard as calling the child X; told-return forms that ask a liking question; worked closes that make a 66 to 75 word turn with the next card (13 turns); an after-key wording that is another angle; an own step's second wording

Harness items found in round d37 (evals only): the off-topic child's answer does not fit the AI question's form; a child answers "pata nahi, aap batao" to a yes/no check-in; closeOffBoard meter rows (0 by hand twice); the meter's mixed-number false key; no rule-based child waits (cause B); the walk driver's stubbed read ("haan" at a yes-or-no card); cardDroppedAfterShortAsk and shareParkUnreturned narrowed readings; aiAsksTold shares tasteNamedIn with the walk, so a mistake in it passes both

md.decisions:
- `dc-r8-director37` (2026-11-25, supersedes `dc-r8-director36`): the decision of director37's judgement (`docs/design/round7/judgements/director37-2026-11-25.md`), seven items. (1) Release 63 is the candidate as run, commit `8354c9855`: six lessons live, class 4 fractions on its rewritten script. **Reverses if** the round's walk puts a wrong mark, a false key or a sentence untrue of its board in front of a child: `node scripts/release.mjs 96007c2 --rollback` (release 62). (2) Lessons: live c4-ch05-t01 (rewritten script, one of two on it), c5-ch02-t01 and c5-ch02-t02 (four passing runs running), c5-ch02-t03, c6-ch06-t01 and c6-ch07-t01 (two of two). Staged: c6-maths-ch07-t03 (three running; live once the row of director36's ruling 6 is fixed and read), c4-maths-ch06-t01 (two of two; live once ruling 4's rows are fixed, read and the live rules pass, `dc-r8-c4-ch06-waits-for-its-script-rows`), c4-maths-ch01-t02 (one of two). The staged batches stay stopped. (3) The next walk change is one thing, the cap: the told answer comes only when every wording of the open part has been said; a hearing after her reply to a side-topic takes the short ask once the question has been heard twice; a fifth hearing on her own does not happen in any form. With it, three small items: one go-on line where a park follows a let-go line (c4 ch01-t02 steady 40); the asked-for picture kept through the card where the figure is the same (`dc-r8-asked-picture-stays-on-same-figure`); credit for the method at a step slip. Built and read as round d37 was, measured on the two topics where it fires. **Reverses if** a pair judge hears a child kept at a question past the point of use. (4) Learning 025 is next, before any further walk round on register: the script rows of director36's mechanism 10 that still stand and this run's rows (`op-r8-d37-learning-025-rows`), answer boards for closing questions, c4-ch06-t01's and c6-ch07-t03's rows. (5) Register (clause 83 fired: 3.5 in nine of nine with every gate line passed): after Learning 025 main writes down what a 4 would sound like from the judges' own words across director30 to director37, and one lesson is rewritten whole to that description and judged against its own director37 lessons. **Reverses if** that lesson scores no higher than 3.5 on register: then register at this gate is taken as the ceiling of scripted turns and the effort goes to what real children show. (6) How a round is read before its run, kept and widened from director36 item 4 (`dc-r8-read-everything-before-a-full-run`). **Reverses if** two rounds running the whole read finds nothing the per-cause reads had not. (7) The harness, evals only, any time: a rule-based child that waits; a steering child not cut at a turn count; the meter's mixed number and its flag on a miss verdict over the card's own board; "nahi" recorded as an acknowledgement (`op-r8-d37-harness-list`). **Why:** nine of nine topics passed every gate line, the first run with no contradiction, misgrade or unsaid board and the first in which the run's own check flagged no row (`ms-r8-director37`); the cap is the one walk fault the round made more likely; register did not move for the eleventh run.
- `dc-r8-d37-reply-turn-ends-on-its-point` (2026-11-25): a turn that opens on her reply to a side-topic (a reply, a park, the AI reply, a return's reply) and has a new point is reply, joint, the whole point and the point's check-in; the card is the next turn (order 054 A(i), design D2; `docs/patches/to-brain/054-director36-the-turns-shape-walk-only.md`). It overrides director29 item 6 and director30 item 3 only for a turn with a new point between the reply and the check-in; a bare reply and check-in stays forbidden and gated. **Why:** director36's one turn ran 66 to 73 words; design D1, ending the reply's turn on its back-to-work line, was heard as a dead turn by both judges of its measure (`rj-r8-go-on-turn-after-a-reply`); D2's turns of 47 to 58 words were judged better than both (`ms-r8-d37-pair-a2`); director37 found it better than director36's in all 36 rows the judges located, in nine of nine topics, 44 to 66 words against 59 to 73. **Reverses if** a run scores register or listening below director36's in two or more topics and names the check-in after a reply: then back to director36's one turn, its length a script matter. Clause set for director37: if three of nine judges fault two check-ins running, the reply's turn after an unanswered check-in ends on its card; director37 found it faulted by none of nine (one called it a mild cost).
- `dc-r8-d37-first-turn-after-two-requests` (2026-11-25): the first teaching turn after two requests is start line, hook, the whole point and its check-in; the card is the next turn (order 054 A(ii), design II-B). **Why:** the first teaching turn was still among a lesson's five worst register rows in five topics for its shape after two give-ups (`dc-r8-register-is-the-turns-shape`); director37's judges heard the split first turn as slow in none of nine. **Reverses if** (the order's A.7) two judges hear it as slow for a child who was ready: then it is split only after two give-ups.
- `dc-r8-d37-clarify-at-held-card` (2026-11-25): a clarify at the check-in of a held card (the card held back to the next turn by `dc-r8-d37-reply-turn-ends-on-its-point`) gets help on the point and the held card in one turn. **Why:** the card is already owed to the child, and a clarify answered with help alone would hold it a second time. **Reverses if:** the round's notes wrote no reversal of its own for this item; it is part of the held-card shape and falls with it, on that decision's reversal condition.
- `dc-r8-d37-wait-says-the-question` (2026-11-25): cause B as ruled six times. Wait one is one short ask; wait two the re-ask (or what wait three is, when that re-ask was just heard); wait three help ending on the question, or on the told step or key when nothing is left; wait four tells; never two turns running with no question; a try-first is always answered as a request, never counted as a wait; the child's words are recorded as said. **Why:** director36 live had a wait with no end (eleven turns in c4 stuck, six in c6-ch07-t01 stuck), largely a harness artefact (`rj-r8-harness-artefact-read-as-the-walk`); after the harness fix no wait in the matrix is longer than two of her turns (`ms-r8-d37-waits-after-harness-fix`); director37: eleven turns to two and six to one, lost in none, over-asked in one lesson (the cap, director37 ruling 1). **Reverses if** (the order's B.7) two judges hear the re-ask as nagging a child who was thinking.
- `dc-r8-pair-measure-flags` (2026-11-25): on a two-topic pair measure a gated flag outside the cause under test is disclosed to the judge, logged and assigned, and does not hold the measure; one inside the cause holds it; no lesson is re-run to clear a flag. **Why:** cause A's second pair run had one gated flag outside the cause (`whyLeadRunning`, steady c6 32, a live opener; `ms-r8-d37-pair-a2`), and re-running to clear it would have spent money on what was not under test. **Reverses if** a disclosed flag is later found to have changed a judge's verdict on the cause.
- `dc-r8-no-pair-run-when-not-exercised` (2026-11-25): a cause the rule-based children do not reach (cause B, the wait) is accepted on an independent review of its predicates and an as-heard read of driven walks, not on a paid pair run. **Why:** no rule-based child waits past a second turn, so a paid run would not hear the change; round d37 accepted causes B and D this way and measured A and C on pairs ($1.33 in all). **Reverses if** a harness child that waits is built (director37 item 7 asks for one).
- `dc-r8-d37-told-answers` (2026-11-25): cause C as kept. C1: an own step's told answer is the step's own answer with its own reason. C2: where a reason names every number of its answer, the told answer is the reason alone; after its measure, also for word answers, teach-backs and number words. C3: at the cap, a named wrong answer's unsaid reason is said with one more try, the turn ending on the question (or on order 049 B4's invitation where the question was said in her two turns before). Correction after the measure: after C1's told own-step answer the worked reason is the next help before "nothing easier". **Why:** the offline matrix showed values said twice in a told answer from 13 to 0, own-step keys without their reason from 2 to 0, the cap before an unsaid named reason from 6 to 0 (`ms-r8-d37-dry-counts-c`); its pair judges said keep with two corrections (`ms-r8-d37-pair-c`); director37: every told answer says its value once, with its reason. **Reverses if** the order's C.7 fires (`docs/patches/to-brain/054-director36-the-turns-shape-walk-only.md`); the notes left the condition to be filled from the pair judges' verdict, which was keep.
- `dc-r8-d37-returns` (2026-11-25): cause D as kept. D1: a return led by a verdict opens on a back-to word where the script has such a form, else the verdict leads as before (pending `returnColdAfterVerdict` counts those rows for Learning). D2: a park of something the child told is always returned to. D3: the AI line never asks what the child's question named; a second taste ask takes the first form not yet answered. No paid pair run: the rule-based children reach D in two topics only, so it was read as heard and reviewed instead. **Why:** D1's fallback without a back-to form made dead turns (`rj-r8-return-fallback-go-on-turn`); director37: every park returned to, the AI line never asks what was named; 17 returns still said cold where the script has no back-to form (a script matter). **Reverses if** (the order's D.7) director37's judges hear the back-to word as one more fixed form in three of nine: then it is dropped and the return waits one turn. It did not fire in director37.
- `dc-r8-read-everything-before-a-full-run` (2026-11-25, supersedes `dc-r8-read-the-walk-before-a-run`, director37 item 6): after the last builder of a round, readers who built nothing read ALL lessons of the final offline walk against the walk the round started from, before the paid run; a rule is kept only on a measure in which it fired; the whole director, brain, evals and script test set runs four at a time after the last builder, not only in CI. The other clauses of `dc-r8-read-the-walk-before-a-run` stand: a fix made after the read is read the same way or does not ship; a sentence said over a board it is untrue of is the script's to cure. **Why:** director36 item 4 asked this only for changed paths, and d37 shows the changed paths are not knowable in advance: three of the four regressions the first whole read found were on paths no pair run or per-cause read had reached (`ms-r8-d37-last-read`); a fixture test failed unseen for two builders (`rj-r8-fixture-walk-not-in-the-builders-test-set`). **Reverses if** two rounds running the whole read finds nothing the per-cause reads had not.
- `dc-r8-plain-no-at-a-check-in` (2026-11-25): a plain "nahi" at any comprehension check-in is "I did not understand" and takes exactly the path "samajh nahi aaya" takes at that check-in (at a bridge: the bridge's easier wording once, then the same check-in; a second goes on); the child's words stay recorded as said; a gated check flags a plain no at a comprehension check-in answered with no help (a stop or a safety turn excepted). A child helped twice at the check-in after a told answer who then says a plain no is let go on kindly, as a third "samajh nahi aaya" is (RULING-G item 2, RULING-H 17a). **Why:** the first whole read found a plain no read as nothing and passed over as a yes in six lessons; the rule-based children had never said it (`rj-r8-harness-child-never-says-no`); director37: served in every case, about 25 rows, no judge hears help forced (clause 85). **Reverses if** a judge hears help forced on a child who meant "no, nothing to ask".
- `dc-r8-d37-try-first-alone` (2026-11-25): every reply to a child's "let me try" is "Haan, pehle tum try karo." and nothing after it, whatever her turn before was; the go-ahead is not a wait turn, and the turn after it is wait one when the child does not answer usefully; a gated check `tryFirstNotAlone` flags a reply that says anything after the go-ahead (it flagged 21 rows of the closing walk and 6 of the round start before the fix and reads 0 after). **Why:** the round's builds had turned 21 of 36 go-aheads into a go-ahead plus a short ask or an invitation (6 before the round), each added to satisfy "never two turns running with no question"; three independent readers faulted it in both whole reads (`rj-r8-rule-satisfied-by-a-tail`); after the fix a re-read found all 36 try-first replies the one line alone, and director37 found every try-first answered with the one line and the child answering next. **Reverses if** two judges hear a child left with nothing to answer after a go-ahead: then the short ask returns only where her turn before had no question.
- `dc-r8-d37-c4-script-back` (2026-11-25): c4-maths-ch05-t01 runs its rewritten script (`6ec62ad79`) with the one wording that failed director36 returned to its director35 text (director36 decision item 2). **Why:** an independent reader read it whole on the final walk and found every sentence true of its board; director37 clause 86: no sentence untrue of its board, and it ships in release 63 (one of two passing runs on it). **Reverses if** (clause 86) its judge finds a sentence untrue of its board: then the release-61 script stays.
- `dc-r8-stuck-turn-12` (2026-11-25): turn 12 of the nine stuck lessons stays as built: help in the point's wording ending on the card's short question, which the help two turns before (turn 8) also ended on, with the card's Hindi form between. Set aside against a reviewer, who read RULING-B5 item 2 (a second help turn ending on a re-ask heard two turns before is nagging) onto it, and asked of the judges by name. **Why:** that ruling was about a waiting child; here the child has said "pata nahi" twice and asked for Hindi once, each a request, each help new; an invitation after help ending "...isliye 1/2" invites the wrong answer 1/2, and the card's question in full would be the longest form twice in six turns; two as-heard readers passed the rows; director37 clause 87: nagging to none of nine. **Reverses if** three of nine judges hear turn 12's question as nagging: then it takes the card's own question where the re-ask was heard in her last two turns.
- `dc-r8-asked-picture-stays-on-same-figure` (2026-11-25, director37 ruling 5): a picture the child asked for after the no-other-drawing line stays through the card where the card's board is the same figure; built in the next walk round (director37 item 3). **Why:** of the judges who met it, two said keeping it was right where it stayed, one that it should have stayed where the card's own board replaced it (c4 ch06-t01 steering 16), and one that giving way was right there (c4 ch01-t02 steering 16, where the picture is the point's own board). **Reverses if** the next walk round's pair judges hear the kept picture as wrong on a card whose board is the same figure (no condition was written with the ruling; this is the measure item 3 sets).
- `dc-r8-c4-ch06-waits-for-its-script-rows` (2026-11-25, director37 ruling 4): c4-maths-ch06-t01 has its two passing runs and does not go live in release 63. **Why:** its judge heard a short reason untrue for the child it was said to (steady 74: "kyunki lagbhag 15 se 20 centimetre" to a child whose accepted answer was 23) and a named wrong answer sent to a remediation about another mistake (stuck 22); both are the script's. **Reverses if** (it lifts when) those rows are fixed and read and the script passes the rules only live scripts are tested against (director36 decision item 2): it goes live in the first release after that.
md.measurements:
- `ms-r8-director37` (2026-11-25): the 37th judged run, the second on a candidate before release (`dc-r8-judge-before-release`). n = 36 lessons: 9 topics (six live scripts, three staged) by 4 rule-based children (steady, stuck, off-topic, steering), Director only, on candidate `8354c9855` (release 62 with round d37's walk and the rewritten class 4 fractions script with its one failed wording put back). 2,862 model calls, about $2.11, 22:27 to 23:12 UTC in one invocation; CI (build and six test shards) and the leak check passed on that tree before the run. Nine Opus judges at high effort, one topic each, by hand, against their director36 reports. **Gate:** nine of nine pass every line, the first run in which all nine pass. 880 keyed answers, every one given a verdict; 0 misgrades (director36: 2), 0 false keys (the meter's one, c5-t01 steady 94, is the meter's again), 0 contradictions, 0 words against a board, 0 unsaid boards; the run's own check exits 0 and flags no row; no safety turn (every teacher row searched for the helpline numbers). **Axes** against director36: listening up in three (c4 ch05-t01 3.5 to 4, c6 ch07-t01 3.5 to 4, c4 ch01-t02 3 to 3.5); worked example c4 ch01-t02 3.5 to 4; screen and speech c4 ch05-t01 and c4 ch01-t02 3.5 to 4; promises c6 ch06-t01 4 to 4.5; register 3.5 in nine of nine, the eleventh run at that score; no axis down in any topic. Length and shape are still the largest register cause: 56 of the 160 register rows that eight reports list by cause. Rulings recorded with the run: in six topics one to three of the stuck, off-topic and steering lessons end a part earlier than in director36, a cost of the round's shape (a point ends on its check-in with the card next; a plain no is answered with help), to be watched with real children (ruling 2); c6 ch07-t03 steady 82, a closing verdict on a cleared screen, is counted 0 and stays on the script list (ruling 3); a judge wrote and deleted a helper script in the scratch folder, nothing in the repository or the run folder changed, its counts stand (ruling 6). Not measured: real children; speech as heard; a waiting child; minutes per lesson now that a point and its card are two turns; an own step told in eight topics, a second AI line, a told side-topic said again at its park; whether a child in production has met the safety turn on a plain answer. Run: `evals/hybrid-side-by-side/results/2026-11-25-director37`. Judgement: `docs/design/round7/judgements/director37-2026-11-25.md`.
- `ms-r8-d37-pair-a` (2026-11-25): cause A, design D1 (the reply's turn ends on its back-to-work line). n = 8 lessons: c5-maths-ch02-t01 and c6-maths-ch07-t01 by the 4 rule-based children, Director only; 577 model calls, $0.42; two Opus judges, one topic each, against their director36 reports. Gates clean; axes unchanged (register 3.5 and 3.5). Turns over 70 words from 6 to 1, over 60 from 63 to 51; the go-on turns after a reply heard as dead in 8 of 8; in the off-topic c5 lesson 31 beats of 43 taught.
- `ms-r8-d37-pair-a2` (2026-11-25): cause A, design D2 (reply, point and check-in; the card next). n = the same 8 lessons, 572 model calls, $0.42; two Opus judges against their director36 reports. Gates clean; axes unchanged. The 8 reply, point and check-in turns (47 to 58 words) judged better than both earlier shapes; turns over 70 words from 6 to 1, over 60 from 63 to 48; check-in endings from 16 to 35; fixed-form rows from 2 to 9; one gated flag outside the cause (`whyLeadRunning`, steady c6 32, a live opener).
